html:
The Ch'ol are a Maya people of northern Chiapas, in southern Mexico, around Tila, Tumbalá, Salto de Agua and Palenque. They speak Ch'ol, one of the Ch'olan languages, the closest living relatives of the language written in Classic Maya script. The map label gives several of their own names for themselves.

In the Classic period their region held great cities such as Palenque, ruled by kings like Pakal. By the time the Spanish came in the 1500s those cities had long been empty, and the Ch'ol lived in farming villages in the hills. Spanish friars moved many into new mission towns. In the 1990s Ch'ol communities took part in the wider Indigenous unrest in Chiapas that included the Zapatista uprising. See also Maya city-states.
